name: Question 1
problem: Find the first three non-zero terms of the Maclaurin expansion of $\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1+x}{1-4x}).$
worked_solution:
First, using the laws of logarithms, we observe that

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1+x}{1-4x}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-4x).\end{aligned}
$$

For the expansion of $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x),$ we recall the standard result

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x) & =x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}-⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

To obtain the expansion of $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-4x),$ we replace $x$ with $-4x$ in the standard expansion:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-4x) & =(-4x)-\frac{(-4x)^{2}}{2}+\frac{(-4x)^{3}}{3}-⋯ \\  & =-4x-8{x}^{2}-\frac{64{x}^{3}}{3}-⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, subtracting the expansion for $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-4x)$ from the expansion for $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1+x}{1-4x}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-4x) \\  & =(x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}-⋯)-(-4x-8{x}^{2}-\frac{64{x}^{3}}{3}-⋯) \\  & =(1+4)x+(-\frac{1}{2}+8){x}^{2}+(\frac{1}{3}+\frac{64}{3}){x}^{3}+⋯ \\  & =5x+\frac{15{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{65{x}^{3}}{3}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Find the first three non-zero terms of the Maclaurin expansion of ln⁡(1+x1−4x).

a
ln⁡(1+x1−4x)=3x+15x22+14x33+⋯
b
ln⁡(1+x1−4x)=x+10x2+15x3+⋯
c
ln⁡(1+x1−4x)=x+3x22+65x33+⋯
d
ln⁡(1+x1−4x)=5x+10x2+15x3+⋯
e
ln⁡(1+x1−4x)=5x+15x22+65x33+⋯
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, using the laws of logarithms, we observe that ln⁡(1+x1−4x)=ln⁡(1+x)−ln⁡(1−4x).

For the expansion of ln⁡(1+x), we recall the standard result ln⁡(1+x)=x−x22+x33−⋯.

To obtain the expansion of ln⁡(1−4x), we replace x with −4x in the standard expansion: ln⁡(1−4x)=(−4x)−(−4x)22+(−4x)33−⋯=−4x−8x2−64x33−⋯.

Finally, subtracting the expansion for ln⁡(1−4x) from the expansion for ln⁡(1+x), we get ln⁡(1+x1−4x)=ln⁡(1+x)−ln⁡(1−4x)=(x−x22+x33−⋯)−(−4x−8x2−64x33−⋯)=(1+4)x+(−12+8)x2+(13+643)x3+⋯=5x+15x22+65x33+⋯
